Or the afternoon stretched thin as paper. The central image could be the bell because it appears at beginning, middle, end. Or perhaps the cup is repeated three times, but the bell appears four times. The central image might be the bell, as a recurring motif that frames the scene.

Also perhaps the motif of time (clock counting nothing, afternoon stretched thin). So we can choose three motifs: auditory signals (bell, clock, train whistle), domestic routine (folding linens, cup, window), and unsaid words/letter (communication, memory). Or we could choose motifs: repetition (bell, cup), nature (pines, wall), time (clock, afternoon). The question says "three motifs". So we need to identify three recurring elements that form motifs. The passage has multiple recurring elements: the bell (repeated), the cup (repeated), the clock (counting nothing), the window (half-open). The letter and train whistle are singular. The pine beyond the wall is a static image.

Thus we could pick motifs: 1) ringing/sonic signals (bell, train whistle, clock). 2) domestic objects (cup, linens, window). 3) intangible communication (letter, words). Or we could pick motifs: 1) repetition (bell, cup). 2) liminality (window half-open, half-open). 3) time (clock, afternoon). But we need to ensure they are motifs, not just random images.

Central image: The bell, as it frames the entire passage, appears at the start, middle (again), and end. It is a central image that signals something, perhaps an event, a memory, a call.

Implied narrative arc: Something about waiting, routine, and perhaps loss or longing. The bell signals the passage of time, perhaps a call that goes unanswered. The domestic scene (folding linens, cup) suggests a woman in a house, perhaps waiting for someone. The letter without sender suggests an unfulfilled communication. The train whistle indicates departure or distance. The words she never said but kept saying anyway suggests unexpressed feelings. The afternoon stretched thin as paper suggests a long, empty day. The bell rings again, perhaps marking the end of something, or a return to the present. So the narrative arc could be: A woman goes through a routine (folding linens, cup) while hearing sounds (bell, train) that evoke a memory or a longing. The letter and unsaid words suggest unresolved communication. The day drags on. The bell rings again, perhaps signifying a moment of reflection or a return to reality.

Thus the summary: central image: the bell; motifs: auditory signals, domestic routine, unsaid words/letter; narrative arc: a woman in a waiting, reflective state, experiencing
